ing: bone-in or boneless, cut in pieces
st: Boil the lentils: put [[1 cup]] red lentils, the turmeric, half the curry leaves and [[2.5 cups]] water in a pot. Simmer for 15 minutes until soft and mushy.
Heat [[1.5 tbsp]] oil in a wide pot. Cook the sliced onion, half the garlic, the ginger and the green chili for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] curry powder and cook for 1 minute, then add the chicken and [[1 tsp]] salt. Stir until coated.
Add half the coconut milk and [[0.5 cup]] water. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the sauce is thick.
Stir the remaining coconut milk and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into the lentils and simmer for 5 minutes. This is the dhal.
Rinse [[2 cups]] rice until the water runs clear. Cook it in [[3 cups]] water with a pinch of salt, covered on low heat, for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Heat [[1.5 tbsp]] oil in a small pan and fry the diced onion, remaining garlic and remaining curry leaves for 4 minutes until browned, then stir this into the dhal.
Serve the rice with the chicken curry and dhal alongside.

ing: roti or paratha, or flour tortillas
st: Stack the flatbreads, cut into thin strips, then cut the strips across into small pieces about an inch long. Set aside.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a very large skillet or wok over high heat. Cook the chicken with [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 6 minutes until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove to a plate.
Add [[1 tbsp]] oil, the onion, garlic and chili. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and carrot with [[1.5 tbsp]] curry powder and the pepper and stir-fry for 3 minutes until just tender.
Push the vegetables aside, add [[1 tbsp]] oil and pour in the eggs. Scramble for 1 minute until set, then mix everything together.
Add the roti pieces, the chicken and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Toss and chop with two metal spatulas for 4 minutes so the bread softens and soaks up the flavor.
Add the soy sauce if using, taste, and serve right away while hot.
Mix [[1 tsp]] yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar in [[0.5 cup]] warm water and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl stir together [[2 cups]] rice flour, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.75 tsp]] salt.
Add the yeast mix, [[1 cup]] coconut milk and about [[1 cup]] warm water. Whisk into a smooth, thin batter like pancake batter.
Cover and let ferment in a warm spot for 2 hours until bubbly and doubled in size.
Heat a small nonstick wok or deep curved pan over medium-high heat and brush lightly with oil.
Pour in about [[0.25 cup]] batter and swirl the pan so it coats the sides and leaves a thicker pool at the bottom.
Crack an egg into the center if you like, cover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the edges are crisp and lacy and the egg is set.
Slide the hopper out carefully and repeat with the rest of the batter. Serve warm.
Put [[2 cups]] rice flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Slowly stir in about [[1.5 cups]] boiling water with a spoon until a soft, warm dough forms.
Cool the dough for a few minutes, then knead until smooth. It should be soft but not sticky.
Oil a string hopper press or a potato ricer, fill it with dough, and press small spirals onto oiled steamer trays or baking parchment.
Set up a steamer with water at a rolling boil.
Steam the trays of spirals for 8 minutes until set and no longer sticky. Keep them covered with a towel.
Meanwhile simmer [[0.5 cup]] red lentils with the turmeric, curry leaves and [[1.5 cups]] water for 15 minutes until soft.
Stir [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk into the lentils, season with salt and cook 3 minutes.
Serve the string hoppers warm with the lentils and a pile of [[0.5 cup]] grated coconut.
Put [[1 cup]] rinsed lentils, [[2.5 cups]] water, the turmeric and the green chili in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add half the onion, half the garlic and half the curry leaves, then simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils collapse.
Stir in [[1 cup]] coconut milk and [[1 tsp]] salt and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Heat [[1.5 tbsp]] oil in a small pan over medium heat and add [[1 tsp]] mustard seeds. Wait until they pop.
Add the dried chilies, remaining onion, garlic and curry leaves and fry for 3 minutes until the onion is golden.
Pour the tempering over the dhal and stir through. Serve with rice or roti.

ing: or tamarind paste for a sour taste
st: Pat the tuna dry and cut it into cubes about 1.5 inches wide.
In a bowl mix [[2 tbsp]] goraka or tamarind paste, [[2 tsp]] pepper, the garlic, the ginger, the turmeric and [[1.5 tsp]] salt into a thick paste.
Toss the tuna in the paste and marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Put the cinnamon stick and half the curry leaves in a wide pot with [[1 tbsp]] oil and heat for 30 seconds.
Add the marinated fish in a single layer, then pour in [[0.75 cup]] water.
Cover and cook on medium-low for 10 minutes.
Uncover, add the remaining curry leaves and cook 10 minutes more, turning the fish gently, until the liquid is gone and the pieces are dark and dry.
Check that the fish is cooked through, then serve with rice.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel. Cut them in half.

Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot, cook half the onion for 4 minutes, add the cinnamon, cloves and [[2 cups]] rice and stir 1 minute. Pour in [[3 cups]] broth with [[1 tsp]] salt, cover, and cook on low for 15 minutes.

For the curry, heat [[1.5 tbsp]] oil, brown the chicken for 5 minutes, then add [[1.5 tbsp]] curry powder, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste and [[0.5 cup]] water. Simmer covered for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Toss the eggplant with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and fry in [[1.5 tbsp]] oil for 8 minutes until browned and soft.
For the sambal, fry the remaining onion in [[1 tbsp]] oil for 6 minutes. Stir in [[1 tsp]] shrimp paste and [[1 tsp]] chili flakes for 1 minute.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Soften banana leaves by passing them briefly over a flame or dipping in hot water, or use a layer of parchment under foil.
On each leaf pile rice, a scoop of chicken curry, eggplant, sambal and two egg halves. Fold up into a tight parcel and secure with foil or string.
Bake the parcels on a tray for 20 minutes. Serve hot, opening the leaf at the table.
If using frozen coconut, thaw it fully and squeeze out extra water.
Put [[1.5 cups]] coconut, [[1.5 tsp]] chili flakes, [[0.75 tsp]] salt and the pepper in a bowl.
Add [[0.25 cup]] chopped red onion and [[1 tbsp]] Maldive fish if using.
Rub everything together with your fingertips for 2 minutes until the coconut turns pink and clumps.
Squeeze in the juice of the lime and mix well.
Taste and add more salt, chili or lime. Serve the same day with rice, hoppers or bread.
Mix [[2 cups]] flour and [[0.75 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add [[0.75 cup]] coconut, [[0.25 cup]] onion, the minced chili and curry leaves, and rub in with your fingers.
Add about [[0.5 cup]] warm water a little at a time and knead into a soft dough, about 3 minutes.
Cover and rest the dough for 15 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls and pat each into a disc about a quarter inch thick on a floured surface.
Heat a dry skillet or griddle over medium-high heat and brush lightly with oil.
Cook each roti for 2 to 3 minutes per side until brown spots appear and it is cooked through, brushing with a little oil.
Keep the finished rotis wrapped in a towel and serve warm with sambol or curry.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Set six ramekins in a deep baking dish.
Warm [[1.5 cups]] coconut milk with [[1 cup]] jaggery over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring until the jaggery dissolves. Cool for 10 minutes.
Lightly beat the 5 eggs in a large bowl, without making foam.
Slowly whisk the warm coconut mixture into the eggs, then add [[0.5 tsp]] cardamom, [[0.25 tsp]] nutmeg and a pinch of salt.
Strain the custard through a fine sieve into a jug for a smooth texture.
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] chopped cashews and divide the custard among the ramekins.
Pour about [[3 cups]] hot water into the baking dish to come halfway up the ramekins and cover loosely with foil.
Bake for 40 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the center. Cool, then chill for 2 hours before serving.
Rinse [[2 cups]] rice well and put it in a heavy pot with [[3 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the water is nearly gone.
Pour in [[1 cup]] thick coconut milk and stir. Cook uncovered on low for 10 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and sticky.
Tip the rice onto a tray or board lined with a damp towel and press it down with a wet spoon into a flat layer about 1 inch thick.
Let it cool for 10 minutes so it firms, then cut into diamonds with a wet knife.
For the onion sambol, heat [[1 tbsp]] oil and cook the onion and chilies for 5 minutes with [[1 tsp]] chili flakes. Add the lime juice off the heat.
Serve the milk rice diamonds with the onion sambol.
Drain the soaked dal and grind half of it to a coarse paste in a food processor, leaving the other half whole.
Mix in the onion, chili, curry leaves, fennel, chili powder and salt to make a thick, grainy dough.
Toss the shrimp with a pinch of chili powder and the lime juice and leave for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil to 350°F in a deep pan. Shape the dough into flat palm-sized patties, about 0.5 inch thick, with a small dent in the center.
Press a few shrimp into the center of each patty. Fry in small batches, turning once, until deep golden and crunchy, about 5 minutes. Shrimp must be opaque and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with lime wedges or a chili sauce.
nt: Best swap: use red lentils soaked 1 hour if you have no chana dal; leave out the shrimp for vegetarian vadai.
